title: Route & Model Latency Dashboard: p50/p95/p99 with streaming vs non-streaming breakdown
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a production-facing Grafana dashboard that surfaces latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) and error rates broken down by model and by API route, with a mandatory split between streaming and non-streaming requests. This ticket covers metric naming, tagging conventions, tracing hook changes to export relevant spans, log/metric pipeline updates, dashboard panels, and alerting thresholds for SLA-sensitive routes.
acceptance_criteria: New metrics emitted: redwood.request.latency_ms histogram and summary with tags: route, model, model_version, streaming (true/false), tier
Tracing hooks updated so request spans include attributes: route, model, model_version, streaming, batch_size. Spans correlate to emitted latency metrics.
Log pipeline adds latency_ms and streaming boolean to request logs; logs are parsable in the ELK/Vector pipeline and available in Explore.

Grafana dashboard created with separate rows: 1) per-model p50/p95/p99 lines; 2) per-route p50/p95/p99 lines; 3) streaming vs non-streaming stacked area or small-multiples; 4) error-rate panels and p99 latency heatmap over last 7/30 days.
Dashboards include quick links to trace view for a selected cell and to the request logs query with filters pre-filled.

Baseline alerts: p99 latency > 500ms for realtime routes (severity P1) and p99 > 1500ms for background routes (severity P2). Alerts fire only for sustained windows (5m) and include query-specified service/model/route tags.
Documentation in Confluence describing metric names, recommended dashboard filters, and instrumentation guide is linked from the dashboard.
Performance overhead of new tracing hooks is validated: tracer overhead < 2% p50 for production QPS synthetic test.
Rollout plan: new metrics/tracing enabled in staging for 48h, then gradual rollout to hosted with canary traffic before enabling for Dedicated/Private.
Unit and integration tests added for the metric tagging logic and log enrichment codepaths.
